newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commercial, hedge sales.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commercial, hedge sales.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower on commercial and hedge selling, traders said.

"There was good commercial selling of the Sep and Nov with crushers buying 500 Sep and 500 Nov. There was good hedging all day and a lot of local selling," a trader said. May WCE futures crush profit margin rose to -11.92 Tuesday from -15.62 Tuesday. May-July spread at $3. Volume was 7,156 lots, or 143,120 tonnes, with 1,000 hedge lots.
Japan bought 3,000-4,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
May canola lost $2.40 to $431.30 and July dipped $3.30 to $433.20. May flax fell $1.10 to $355, July rose $1 to $355 on commercials.
July western barley ended $1.50 lower at $140.50 on commercial selling with locals and commission houses buying. May-July spread at $0.50. Volume was 750 lots. Oats did not trade.
May feed wheat sank $3 to $168 on commission and local selling as Alberta Wheat Pool bought, traders said. Sixty May-July spread at $2, 25 May-Oct $3. Volume 800 lots.
UGG sold five July feed pea contracts down US$0.50 at US$191.50 and bought five December down US$0.40 at US$191.10.
(All values in Canadian dollars a tonne except feed peas)
